shifts.summary: The shift was overall reported as moderate. Reasoning was mixed, with many diagram and statement questions and no coding‑decoding types. GA was generally easy, covering current affairs and constitutional articles. Quant was lengthy with heavy data‑interpretation and arithmetic, causing time pressure. English was the hardest section, featuring long comprehension and vocabulary items.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported a mix of easy and moderate difficulty, noting many diagram‑based and statement questions and the absence of coding‑decoding types. Some found the paper lengthy and skipped a few items due to time pressure.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GK was generally reported as easy or okay, with current affairs and history items and some logical fixed‑answer questions. Candidates found it doable.

topics.topic: Article 3 – power to alter state boundaries

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Candidates found math hard and lengthy, with many calculative DI and geometry questions. Time pressure was high, leading to skipping strategies and difficulty completing within the allotted time.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was reported as difficult with lengthy comprehension and vocabulary items, though spelling questions were easier. Some candidates found the passage easy and attempted all questions.

intro: On 14 October 2026, the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, with mixed reasoning, a lengthy quantitative section, and English identified as the hardest part; candidates reported good attempts in the range of 60–82, though these figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts. Shift 2 was described as easy to moderate overall, with reasoning easy, general awareness and quantitative sections moderate, and English easy to moderate; about 18 questions were attempted well, also unofficial. Shift 3 is still pending a usable analysis, and further candidate evidence is required before publishing details.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 was reported as moderate overall, while Shift 2 was described as easy to moderate. No analysis is available yet for Shift 3, so its difficulty level cannot be confirmed at this time.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as most challenging on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: In Shift 1, English was noted as the hardest section, and the quantitative section was lengthy and time‑pressuring. In Shift 2, English was considered easy to moderate, but time pressure affected the general knowledge and current affairs items.

faqs.q: How many questions were reported as well‑attempted on 14 October 2026?
faqs.a: Candidates in Shift 1 reported good attempts in the range of 60–82, and candidates in Shift 2 reported about 18 well‑attempted questions. These numbers are unofficial and should be treated as indicative only.

faqs.q: Is there any analysis available for Shift 3 of the 14 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: No usable analysis has been published for Shift 3 yet. More candidate evidence is needed before a detailed review can be provided.

faqs.q: Does SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the 14 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: Yes, SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure comparability of results.
